newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM SAYS NOT ALL NAZI-STOLEN GOLD TRACED.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM SAYS NOT ALL NAZI-STOLEN GOLD TRACED.

text.p: Belgium said on Monday its National Bank fully recuperated gold stolen from it by nazis during World War II, but it was unclear what happened to gold stolen from private persons and Jews in particular.
Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said in an answer to questions from parliamentarians, "So far no traces of these assets have been found in the (central bank's) capital."

Maystadt is setting up a commission to investigate what happened to Jewish assets which were not returned to their rightful owners. Reportedly, the assets had been returned to the Belgian government, but nothing was found, he said.
Between June 1940 and September 1944 the German Reichsbank received 6.4 tonnes of gold from private persons, the minister said, adding the whereabouts of the gold was unknown.
A U.S. senator -- Alfonse D'Amato -- has alleged the Swiss National Bank knew that 100 tonnes of gold it took from Germany's wartime government had been stolen from Belgium.
The Swiss central bank has said it was unclear if it knew at the time where the gold came from.
